Rae: Heads-up - after rolling the kernel-picker heuristic to canary this morning host CPU tail climbed. p99 +10%. GPU unaffected.

Jon: can you share the quick perf/kern trace?

Priya: pasted a 30s perf sample from the canary box. top funcs:
```
# perf top -p <pid>
 22.6% tokenize::tokenize_and_slice
 18.9% http2::encode_hpack
 15.3% small_frame_emitter::writev_emit
 11.0% kv_cache::ensure_shard_bound
 5.4% grpc::writev
```

Sam: kv_cache::ensure_shard_bound suggests kernels are moving short requests to workers without the shard pinned -> extra shard binds/evicts + more proto unmarshal work. That increases tiny writes and HPACK CPU.

Anya: repro locally with short-seq load (2k rps): selector set to opt-lowlat -> avg write syscalls/request = 3.8 vs baseline 1.0; kv-hit drops ~9% during the first 45s. tcpdump shows many small http2 DATA frames (<=256B).

Rae: hmm. two-pronged approach: reduce syscall & HPACK churn, and reduce KV shard remaps. Proposals: (A) ingress write coalescer (merge small token frames up to N within M ms), (B) selector "warmup affinity" so first K requests prefer kernels with shard residency, (C) short-seq batch watermark bump to reduce mini-switching, (D) a lightweight host tokenizer pool to amortize tokenization syscall cost.

Jon: i like A+B. D is more invasive but could help CPU and avoid extra syscall churn by doing tokenization in a pooled worker with fewer syscall transitions.

Anya: ingress coalescer sketch: coalesce up to 6 frames, max_delay_ms=2, max_bytes=8192. That should drop writev/sec by ~60% on local run. Caveat: single-request p50 might add ~0.8-1.5ms. We'll gate by p95.

Sam: warmup affinity idea: when a flow is new, prefer kernels whose 'kv_shard_residency_score' > threshold for first N requests (configurable). Also surface metric kernel.kv_local_hit_pct. This avoids remapping hot keys to cold kernels during warmup.

Priya: quick numbers from a 5m A/B run locally: control=v2 baseline, variant=v2+affinity+coalesce: writev/sec -58%, kv-evict-rate -11% in warmup window, host p99 -9%. single-request p50 +1.2ms (within acceptable limit).

Rae: nice. can we get flamegraphs + syscall traces for the A/B run and upload to perf?

Anya: uploading now: https://perf.redwood/trace/5812345678/ab-run. included tcpdump for HPACK ops.

Jon: small note: coalescer must be careful with flow control and backpressure - don't break streaming semantics for large requests. Add heuristics: only coalesce frames marked as token-chunk and short (<512B).

Sam: agree. also add a fallback: if ingress coalescer sees p95 latency creep >5% during canary, auto-disable. Rollout gate.

Priya: added metrics we need on the dashboard: kernel.kv_local_hit_pct, ingress.writev_per_request, http2.hpack_encode_ops/sec, host.syscall.writev/sec. Add alerts: kv-evict-rate +5% and writev/sec +100% during rollouts.

perf-bot: [alert] Canary kernel-picker change -> host CPU p99 +10%, kv-evict-rate +8%, writev/sec +165%. TraceID: 5812345678. Suggested mitigations: warmup affinity, ingress frame coalesce, batch watermark tuning.

Rae: immediate actions:
- rollback canary to old picker for 30m (Jon)
- spin up A/B with variant including affinity + coalesce (Anya + Sam)
- collect full flame + syscall traces for both groups (Priya)
- add dashboard panels & alerts (Rae)

Jon: rolling rollback now, will post metrics in 10m.

Jon: rollback done. baseline metrics back within 12 minutes. holding for 20m then will start A/B.

Anya: PR incoming with coalescer behind a flag + unit/e2e test that asserts streaming correctness. Also adding microbench that reports writev counts and hpack ops.

Sam: ill add affinity heuristic in kernel-picker; default N=16 requests for warmup pin. We'll make it configurable and opt-in.

Rae: schedule follow-up sync 2026-03-24 16:00 UTC. owners: Anya (ingress coalesce), Sam (kernel affinity + batch watermark), Priya (perf harness), Jon (canary ops). PERF ticket created PERF-2009. Keep updates here. :thumbsup:
